agent_notes: בֵּרַכְנוּכֶם has a plural 'you' while הַבָּא is singular: the Hebrew shifts from the one who comes to the group addressed. אִסְרוּ־חַג בַּעֲבֹתִים is genuinely disputed. The literal layer keeps 'bind the festival with thick cords/boughs' and brackets nothing in, because Hebrew has no word for 'sacrifice'. Rashi, Radak, Ibn Ezra, Meiri and Metzudat David take חַג as the festival offering, bound with ropes up to the altar horns; the Targum has a bound lamb. BBE ('let the holy dance be ordered with branches') reflects the other reading, עֲבֹת as leafy boughs (cf. Ezek 6:13, 'leafy tree'), a procession. I chose cords in the glosses and described both in the commentary. The 'leafy boughs' parallel is my own reading, not drawn from a packet commentary.

STEPBible glosses אֵל as '[is] God' and entity deity.yhwh; I kept 'God' and glossed יְהוָה separately, reading 'God [is] YHWH' as a confession of identity. KJV 'which hath shewed us light' turns the Hebrew's separate clause 'and he gave light to us' into a relative clause; I keep the clause. The Hebrew וַיָּאֶר is a past/perfective narrative form, so 'gave light'.
The versions render חֶסֶד 'mercy' (KJV), 'kindness' (YLT), 'lovingkindness' (ASV). I used 'covenant loyalty' in the gloss and 'steadfast love' in the dramatic layer, and 'loyal love' in the literal.
